responsibilities: Full accountability for the LookML codebase, including expert-level query performance tuning and optimization within Looker-specific constraints
End-to-end responsibility for SQL and Python scripts. This includes navigating SQL Server environments to manage the tables and views that power Looker models.
Rigorous peer code reviews in GitHub to maintain high-quality standards.
Balance "Business as Usual" (BAU) support and troubleshooting with the development of long-term product features and releases.
Partner closely with Engineering to ensure seamless product deployments and feature rollouts.
Translate complex data logic into clear, actionable answers for non-technical stakeholders and act as a technical escalation point for client queries.
Work synchronously with Database Analyst, Cloud Engineering, Engineering, and Product teams to ensure technical alignment and operational excellence.
Lead upskilling sessions and maintain a "positive mindset" toward documentation, ensuring the team remains scalable and well-informed.
A drive to master emerging technologies and keep pace with industry trends.
Meticulous approach to data validation, code integrity, and documentation.
Foster a culture of continuous learning within the team.
End-to-End Reporting: Gather stakeholder requirements, guide DWH developers on table structures, and implement polished visualizations in Tableau.

Architect’s Partner: Define functional requirements for the Data Warehouse. While you won’t build the pipelines, you will guide Star Schema design to ensure optimization for high-performance reporting.
Metrics Governance: Take full ownership of the JobAdder "Metric Store." Lead the sign-off process to ensure definitions are consistent across all departments.
Root-Cause Investigation: Use advanced SQL profiling to perform deep-dive audits and investigate why "the numbers don't look right," bridging the gap between business expectations and raw data.
Documentation & KT: Maintain rigorous documentation for governed metrics. You believe a dashboard is only as good as the metadata behind it.
